title: RFP Hub schema metaschema
description: Constrains the shape of opportunity.schema.json itself and legalises the x- annotation keywords the standard uses on top of the 2020-12 vocabulary. This is deliberately NOT a JSON Schema $vocabulary or a custom dialect — the standard is an application schema, not a schema language. It exists so the annotations are a machine-checked contract rather than a convention, and so nobody hand-edits one into an invalid shape. Validate the schema file against this in CI.
$comment: Only three x- keywords exist, and each earns its place by expressing something 2020-12 cannot. Anything 2020-12 CAN express must use the standard keyword: `deprecated`, `examples`, `$comment`, `default`, `readOnly` and `writeOnly` are all native and must never be re-invented with an x- prefix.

$schema.description: The dialect is pinned. Never alias it to 'latest' — the dialect choice is extremely sticky once publishers have tooling.

$id.description: Stamped from spec.config.json by codegen; never hand-edited.

additionalProperties.description: The top level is closed; unknown keys are rejected. There is no extension mechanism — a new field requires a spec release.

annotations.description: The annotation keywords any schema object in our file may carry: the native 2020-12 metadata keywords we rely on, plus the three x- extensions.

deprecated.description: THE NATIVE 2020-12 DEPRECATION FLAG, and the machine-readable one. Any deprecated element sets `deprecated: true` here; generic tooling that knows nothing about this standard still sees it. `x-deprecated` may accompany it but never replaces it — see dependentRequired above.

$comment.description: Editorial note for maintainers of this schema. Not for consumers, and not rendered into the generated field reference — that is what `description` is for. Design rationale, deliberate omissions and traps a future editor might 'fix' belong here.

examples.description: Native 2020-12 annotation: an array of valid instance values for this element. Non-normative and non-validating — an example is an illustration, not a constraint. Prefer them on any element whose shape is not obvious from its type.

x-stability.description: 'stable' = the element is expected to survive unchanged. 'provisional' = accepted on single-source evidence or otherwise at risk; it may change or be withdrawn without the ceremony a stable element would get. ABSENCE MEANS 'stable': the document root declares `x-stability: stable` and every element inherits that unless it says otherwise, so only the at-risk elements are annotated.

x-since.description: The spec version in which this schema element was introduced. 2020-12 has no native equivalent.

since.description: The spec version in which this element was deprecated.

replacedBy.description: Path or name of the successor element, or null when there is none.

note.description: Why it was deprecated and what a publisher should do instead.

x-deprecated.description: Carries ONLY the deprecation metadata 2020-12 cannot express: which version deprecated the element, what replaces it, and why. The deprecation itself is signalled by the native `deprecated: true`, which this keyword requires — it is a supplement, never a substitute. Elements removed outright are recorded in the release's field mapping table in CHANGELOG.md instead.

annotatedSchema.description: Any subschema in our file: an object schema (which may carry the annotations above) or the boolean form.

description.description: Every named element in our schema carries a description; the field reference is generated from them.
